programs.title: Foundations
programs.goal: Basic facts about operators, states, energy and ground energy that every later argument uses.
programs.wanted: Lemmas that a later program visibly needs. Not restatements of Mathlib, and not variations of lemmas already in the record.

programs.title: Locality and tensor structure
programs.goal: How operators on different sets of qubits or qudits combine: products, commutation, supports, and operators built from smaller ones.
programs.wanted: Closure properties of QActsOn, embedding an operator on few qudits into many, and how energy behaves for operators on disjoint supports.

programs.title: Classical constraint problems as Hamiltonians
programs.goal: The bridge to the classical PCP theorem: a constraint satisfaction problem is a diagonal normalized Hamiltonian whose ground energy counts violated constraints.
programs.wanted: Sums of diagonal terms, ground energy as the minimum number of violated constraints, and classical instances as RelYes and RelNo instances.

programs.title: Manipulating the promise gap
programs.goal: Operations on normalized Hamiltonians that preserve or change the relative gap in a controlled way: rescaling, padding with trivial terms, repeating terms, and changing locality bounds.
programs.wanted: For each operation, a lemma giving the new term count and bounds on the new ground energy in terms of the old.

programs.title: Commuting and frustration-free Hamiltonians
programs.goal: Hamiltonians whose terms commute, or whose ground energy is zero: the simplest quantum instances, and the setting of the known special cases of the conjecture.
programs.wanted: Definitions are not open to contributors yet, so state lemmas directly in terms of Commute and groundEnergyOn.

programs.title: A formal statement of the conjecture
programs.goal: Define quantum verification (QMA), reductions, and the promise problem, and state the quantum PCP conjecture in Lean.
programs.wanted: Closed to proposals. This needs new definitions, which must be written and reviewed by a specialist in Hamiltonian complexity.

programs.title: Known theorems
programs.goal: Formalize established results around the conjecture, such as QMA-completeness of the local Hamiltonian problem and the NLTS theorem.
programs.wanted: Closed until the statement program has the definitions these theorems are about.

barriers.name: Low-energy trivial states
barriers.test: Do the proposed hard instances have a low-energy state that a constant-depth circuit can prepare? If so, that circuit is a classical witness, the instances are in NP, and the approach cannot give QMA-hardness. Hard instances must come from a family with no low-energy trivial states.
barriers.source: Anshu, Breuckmann, Nirkhe, NLTS Hamiltonians from Good Quantum Codes

barriers.name: Product-state approximation
barriers.test: Do the proposed hard instances live on interaction graphs where product states are known to approximate the ground energy well, such as graphs of high degree? Then the approximation problem for them is in NP and the approach cannot work as stated.
barriers.source: Brandão, Harrow, Product-state Approximations to Quantum Ground States

barriers.name: Commuting Hamiltonians in NP
barriers.test: Are the proposed hard instances commuting Hamiltonians in a class already known to be in NP, such as 2-local commuting Hamiltonians or commuting Hamiltonians on locally expanding graphs? Then they cannot be QMA-hard unless QMA equals NP.
barriers.source: Aharonov, Eldar, The commuting local Hamiltonian on locally-expanding graphs is in NP

barriers.name: Relativization
barriers.test: Would the argument go through unchanged relative to any oracle? Proofs of quantum PCP statements cannot relativize, so an approach built only from relativizing steps cannot succeed.
barriers.source: Buhrman, Helsen, Weggemans, Quantum PCPs: On Adaptivity, Multiple Provers and Reductions to Local Hamiltonians
